docs.purpose: Completes an admin's two-factor setup by checking the six-digit code from their authenticator app; on success it upgrades their login session to a higher trust level and issues one-time backup codes for use if they lose their device.
docs.data_story: It touches no table at all and writes `admin_backup_codes` and `admin_audit_log`. Its response is an explicit pick-by-name projection of 2 fields, so a column added to a table upstream does not leak into the client by accident. It is called from 1 place: `src/features/admin-security/api/useAdminSecurity.ts`.
docs.under_126: Becomes a **CONTRACT descriptor** of archetype `MUTATION`. It declares `database.writes[]` with a `write_discipline` per target (the Spec 122 vocabulary verbatim), its idempotency posture, its optimistic contract and its rollback. Its `consumers[]` becomes the edge list of the fan-out graph — the join nothing in this estate holds today.

notes: writeAdminAudit is called for 'mfa_enrolled' after backup codes are issued. Challenge/verify goes through Supabase Auth (GoTrue), not a raw table read. replaceBackupCodes deletes all existing rows for the user and inserts 10 fresh hashed rows in one transaction. An audit-write failure here is deliberately swallowed (logged, not thrown) because the factor is already verified and the codes already stored — a 500 would strand a live enrollment and hide the one-time plaintext codes. Requires authMethod === 'session'. | MEASURED 2026-09-15: FINDINGS. (1) CENSUS DISAGREEMENT: census_reads is [] for this route, but it DOES read — `profiles` on every request through verifyAdminAuth (src/lib/auth/verify-admin.ts:117-120), and `admin_backup_codes` through consumeBackupCode when ADMIN_MFA_ENFORCED='true' (src/lib/admin/backup-codes.ts:116). census_writes [admin_backup_codes, admin_audit_log] is confirmed; the admin_backup_codes write is a DELETE+10×INSERT pair inside one transaction (src/lib/admin/backup-codes.ts:72-81), not a single statement. (2) Audit failure swallowed at :98-103 with the reason stated at :99-101 — deliberate, so a caller cannot tell an audited enrollment from an unaudited one. (3) The 10 PLAINTEXT backup codes are returned in the body at :106 — by design (:83-85), stored only as sha256(salt:code) (src/lib/admin/backup-codes.ts:52-56). (4) NO RATE LIMIT on a 6-digit TOTP verify endpoint (:72-76). Brute-force resistance is entirely delegated to Supabase GoTrue; nothing in this repo throttles :44. Worth a reviewer's attention even though the code path is deliberate. (5) Backup-code hashing uses sha256, not a KDF — src/lib/admin/backup-codes.ts:16-24 argues the case explicitly (64-bit server-generated one-time codes). Comment, not evidence; the code is at :52-56. (6) No SELECT *; all SQL parameterised. | Caching: none observed — no Cache-Control, revalidate, dynamic or in-process cache in the file. | Other guards / classification: CSRF Origin allowlist (POST is a MUTATING_METHOD) via src/lib/auth/verify-admin.ts:45 + :70-78, default-deny at :336. MFA aal2 gate src/lib/auth/verify-admin.ts:143-173, inert unless ADMIN_MFA_ENFORCED='true'. TOTP challenge/verify is done server-side against GoTrue at :63 and :72-76 — the 6-digit code is never compared in this repo. | No test file under src/tests/** imports this route.
